gaps.sentence: She couldn't resist ___ the last biscuit.
Could you help me ___ these boxes upstairs?
gaps.explanation: help takes a bare infinitive or to-infinitive: help me (to) carry. Both accepted.

gaps.sentence: I can't wait ___ you the photos.
gaps.explanation: can't wait + to-infinitive: can't wait to show.

gaps.sentence: I like ___ up early in summer.
gaps.explanation: With 'like' meaning enjoy, -ing is preferred: like getting up. 'Would like' takes to: I'd like to get up.

gaps.sentence: She forgot ___ the email, so she sent it twice.
gaps.explanation: forget + -ing = lose the memory of a past action (she did send it).

gaps.sentence: I look forward to ___ your suggestions at the meeting.
When I was a student, I used ___ in shared flats.
gaps.explanation: used TO + infinitive = past habit/state: used to live. (Compare: be used to living.)
seem/appear take the to-infinitive: seems to know.
